preconditions.expression: n >= 3 and m >= 2 and m < n
preconditions.description: The number of towns n is at least 3, and the number of monasteries m is at least 2 and strictly less than n.

preconditions.expression: len(monasteries) == m and all(1 <= town <= n for town in monasteries) and len(set(monasteries)) == m
preconditions.description: The monasteries list contains exactly m distinct town indices between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b and 1 <= c <= 1000 for a, b, c in edges)
preconditions.description: The edges form a tree with n-1 bidirectional roads, each with a positive integer length between 1 and 1000.

postconditions.description: The output consists of two integers: the maximum number of pilgrims Walter can make unhappy and the number of towns (not monasteries) whose destruction achieves this maximum.

postconditions.expression: max_unhappy == max(sum(all(farthest_monasteries[p] == [] for p in pilgrims) for town in non_monastery_towns if destroy(town)))
postconditions.description: max_unhappy is the maximum number of pilgrims that can be made unhappy by destroying exactly one non-monastery town, where a pilgrim is unhappy if all their farthest monasteries become unreachable after the destruction.

postconditions.expression: num_ways == sum(1 for town in non_monastery_towns if sum(all(farthest_monasteries[p] == [] for p in pilgrims) for p in pilgrims) == max_unhappy)
postconditions.description: num_ways is the count of non-monastery towns whose destruction results in exactly max_unhappy unhappy pilgrims.
